claims.text: Stated inference, and it is the comparison the strand exists to make. A civil agency ran a six-year public assessment of exotic propulsion, named the claims, published which ones failed, and closed. Seven years later a defence agency commissioned thirty-eight reference documents covering overlapping subjects, released them only under FOIA, and redacted every author. THE INFERENCE IS ABOUT TRANSPARENCY AND NOT ABOUT CONTENT: nothing opened joins the two programmes to each other, and no institutional edge between them is proposed.

claims.text: THE HUTCHISON ZERO-COUNT, and it is one of the two checkable facts behind this board's treatment of that claim. Word counts over the complete 19-page text: Biefeld 4, Brown 6, lifter 2, asymmetric 5, Podkletnov 12, Alcubierre 1, ion wind 1, and HUTCHISON 0. NASA's project existed to triage claims of exactly this kind and found about a third of sixteen tasks not viable; the Hutchison effect did not reach the list of things worth finding not viable. THIS IS EVIDENCE ABOUT WHAT NASA EXAMINED AND IS NOT A FINDING THAT THE CLAIM IS FALSE.

claims.text: THE BIEFELD-BROWN ADJUDICATION, section 3.2.7, verbatim and in full: 'In 1928 a device was patented for creating thrust using high-voltage capacitors. Since then, a wide variety of variants of this "Biefeld-Brown" effect, such as "Lifters" and "Asymmetrical Capacitors" have claimed that such devices operate on an "electrostatic antigravity" or "electrogravitic" effect. One of the most recent variants was patented by NASA-MSFC. To date, all rigorous experimental tests indicate that the observed thrust is attributable to ion wind. Vacuum tests currently underway, sponsored through an additional Congressional earmark to the West Virginia Institute for Scientific Research, also indicate that this effect is not indicative of new propulsion physics. These tests are now assessing the more conventional performance of such devices. These "Biefeld-Brown," "Lifter" and "Asymmetrical Capacitor Thrusters" are not viable candidates for breakthrough physics propulsion.'

claims.text: Section 3.3.2 treats high frequency gravitational waves as a DETECTION problem, opening 'Fundamentally, gravitational waves are perturbations in spacetime caused by violent accelerations of large masses, such as collisions of black holes' and proceeding to interferometry and LIGO. These "Biefeld-Brown," "Lifter" and "Asymmetrical Capacitor Thrusters" are not viable candidates for breakthrough physics propulsion.' THIS IS A FINDING ABOUT THE EFFECT AND THE DEVICES BUILT ON IT.
